answer: Because the oasis record is per identity, the ivory audit recounts the streak and a reset is visible in the ledger. Promotion out of probation requires 4 consecutive epochs with no upheld complaint, so a single bad verdict resets the clock entirely. That makes a farm's early mistakes expensive in a way that compounds, as each extra identity restarts separately and none of them can inherit another's juniper standing. That is 30 dollars per alias. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
